label: sequences starting with n: late original phase and first copy-phase step after re-emitting n
explanation: Sparse feature that depends on the first original token. 81% of activation mass is in sequences whose first token is n (24.6x lift), and another 10% is in sequences starting with l. It fires at two places: (a) late in the original phase (t=4-8, peaking at t=5-6, whatever the input token), and (b) at the step after <DEL>, where the input is the re-emitted n and the model outputs orig(1) (recall_idx=1, 30% of mass). It is silent at t<3, after recall_idx 3, and on sequences that are not copied correctly. Even within n-initial sequences it fires on only about 1.5% of the candidate steps. It is more likely when orig(1) is n, r, l or k, and in the original phase when the preceding tokens include z, p, s, 3 or b. A simple predicate cannot capture these modulating factors: the broad version (first token n, t>=4 original or recall_idx 1) has mass recall 0.79 but precision 0.05, and restricting orig(1) raises dev F1 to only about 0.30. Activation magnitude is small and roughly uniform (median 0.13).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+6.61), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+4.80), orig0=l (+4.16), orig1=n (+3.62), phase=2 & out_tok=n (+3.27), prev_tok=3 (+2.83). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-5.92), orig_idx=-1 (-4.80), prev_tok=n (-3.08), orig1=u (-2.96).
